historical_record.description: Under the 1947 recreation bond program the Recreation and Park Commission engaged C. F. Strothoff, architect, to design improvements to Margaret S. Hayward Playground ($100,000) and bleachers ($50,000).

The Recreation and Park Commission awarded the contract for improvements to Margaret Hayward Playground to Martinelli Construction Co. at $283,973, the second-lowest bid, rejecting the low bid because its proposal form had been altered.

The Recreation and Park Commission resolved that the Laguna Street side of the playground keep the name of Margaret S. Hayward, and named its softball field James P. Lang Field, for the department's former general manager, one of the first presidents of the American Softball Association.

The Recreation and Park Commission approved the design of a new multi-purpose recreation center at Margaret Hayward Playground by Beverly Willis and Associates, architects, presented by the firm's Elizabeth Gibbons.
